# SPI Host Core FSM Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the core finite-state-machine behavior of an SPI host. It is responsible for:

- Accepting command segment descriptors.
- Controlling the SPI clock and chip-select signals.
- Generating the control pulses needed to shift data out and sample data in.
- Implementing SPI timing requirements such as lead, trail, and idle delays.
- Supporting back-to-back command segments without deasserting chip-select when required.
- Stalling cleanly when the transmit or receive datapath is not ready.

The module does not store TX or RX data itself. It only requests bytes from the transmit side and delivers received bytes to the receive side using ready/valid-style handshakes.

## 2. Reset, Enable, and Software Reset

### Hardware Reset

When the hardware reset is asserted, the module shall:

- Enter the ordinary idle state.
- Drive all chip-select outputs inactive (high).
- Drive the SPI clock to its idle level.
- Deassert the active status.
- Clear all transfer progress counters.

After reset, the module shall be ready to accept a command when enabled.

### Module Enable

The module has a global enable input.

- When the enable is deasserted, the module shall not accept commands.
- When the enable is deasserted during an active transaction, the module shall freeze all state: no SPI clock edges, no chip-select changes, no counter updates, and no data-control pulses.
- When the enable is reasserted, the module shall resume from the exact point at which it was stopped.

### Software Reset

A software reset input shall have the same effect as returning the module to its ordinary idle state:

- Any in-progress segment is abandoned.
- All chip-select outputs are driven inactive.
- The SPI clock is returned to its configured idle level.
- The active status is cleared.
- Transfer counters are cleared.

Software reset shall not otherwise alter the stored configuration or command parameters.

## 3. Command Acceptance

A command segment is accepted only when:

- The module is enabled.
- The module asserts its command-ready output.
- The command-request input is asserted.
- No stall condition is active.

When a command is accepted, the module shall capture:

- The target chip-select identifier.
- The timing and clock configuration associated with that chip select.
- The segment length, direction, speed, and chip-select-active-after-transaction flag.

A command request presented while the module is not ready shall have no effect during ordinary active operation. The one exception is the chip-select-active wait state described in Section 8.

### Ready Behavior

The module shall assert command-ready in the following situations:

- In the ordinary idle state.
- While waiting with chip-select held active and no segment currently transferring, provided the next command targets the same chip-select.
- At the end of the post-transaction idle delay, so that a command request already waiting can be accepted immediately without an extra idle-state cycle.

The module shall not assert command-ready while a segment is actively transferring data, except on the final timeslice of a chip-select-active segment when a same-chip-select continuation segment is already being presented.

Command-ready shall be suppressed whenever a stall condition is active.

## 4. SPI Clock Generation

The module generates the SPI clock using a divided version of the module clock.

- A clock-divider field selects the number of core clock cycles in one SPI half-period.
- If the divider value is N, the effective half-period is N + 1 core clock cycles.
- The finite-state machine advances once per SPI half-period boundary when active.

The SPI clock output shall idle at the configured polarity:

- When CPOL is 0, the idle level is low.
- When CPOL is 1, the idle level is high.

During data or dummy cycles, the SPI clock shall toggle between its two active levels, producing pulses with the configured polarity. The clock shall remain at the idle level during:

- Chip-select lead time.
- Chip-select trail time.
- Inter-command idle time.
- Configuration-switch delay.
- Chip-select-active wait time.
- Any stall or disabled condition.

No SPI clock edges shall be generated while all chip-select outputs are inactive.

## 5. SPI Clock Phase and Data Timing

The module shall support CPHA 0 and CPHA 1.

- With CPHA 0, the first bit of a transmitting segment is launched when the chip-select lead phase completes and the transfer begins.
- With CPHA 1, data launch is delayed until the first SPI clock edge.
- The module shall generate sample-enable and shift-enable pulses at the times appropriate for the selected phase.

The module shall also support full-cycle sampling.

- In full-cycle mode, incoming data is sampled one full SPI clock period after the data-launch edge, rather than one half-period later.
- Full-cycle mode affects only the timing of the sample-enable output. It shall not change SPI clock generation, chip-select timing, or shift-enable timing.

## 6. Chip-Select Control

The module shall drive one active-low chip-select output per chip-select line.

During normal operation, exactly one chip-select output shall be active low while a transaction is in progress.

The chip-select output for the selected target shall be asserted low during:

- Chip-select lead time.
- All data or dummy clock cycles.
- Chip-select trail time.
- The chip-select-active wait state.

All chip-select outputs shall be high during:

- The ordinary idle state.
- The inter-command idle delay.
- The configuration-switch delay.

The module shall not assert a chip-select output while the SPI clock is toggling.

### Lead, Trail, and Idle Delays

The module shall implement three programmable timing delays, measured in SPI half-periods:

- Chip-select lead time: the delay between the falling edge of chip-select and the first SPI clock edge.
- Chip-select trail time: the delay between the last SPI clock edge and the rising edge of chip-select.
- Inter-command idle time: the minimum time that all chip-select lines remain high between transactions.

For each timing field, the actual number of half-periods shall be one greater than the programmed field value. For example, a programmed value of zero gives one half-period of delay.

## 7. Segment Execution

Each accepted command segment has a direction, speed, and length.

### Direction

The module shall support four direction classes:

- **Dummy**: no data is transmitted or received. The module only produces SPI clock cycles.
- **TX only**: data is transmitted from the transmit side. Incoming data is ignored.
- **RX only**: data is received and delivered to the receive side. The data lines are not driven by the host.
- **Bidirectional**: data is transmitted and received simultaneously. This is only valid in Standard SPI mode.

### Speed

The module shall support three speed modes:

- **Standard**: one data line is driven and one data line is sampled. Each shift advances by one bit.
- **Dual**: two data lines are used. Each shift advances by two bits.
- **Quad**: four data lines are used. Each shift advances by four bits.

The current speed mode shall be reported to the datapath so that the shift register can select the correct shift width and data-line mapping.

### Segment Length

The length field in a command segment is encoded as a count minus one.

- For TX, RX, and bidirectional segments, it represents the number of data bytes.
- For dummy segments, it represents the number of dummy clock cycles.

The module shall track the progress of the current segment and determine when the current byte or dummy cycle is the last one.

### Transmit Handshake

At the start of each transmitted byte, the module shall issue a transmit-byte request.

- The module shall only issue this request when the transmit side is ready.
- If the transmit side is not ready, the module shall assert the transmit-stall status and hold all outputs and progress until the transmit side becomes ready.
- The transmit-byte request shall be suppressed during stalls.

For the final transmitted byte of a segment, the module shall accompany the transmit request with an end-of-segment marker. This marker shall indicate that any partially used transmit word should be flushed and that no further bytes are needed for this segment.

### Receive Handshake

At the end of each received byte, the module shall issue a receive-byte request.

- The module shall only issue this request when the receive side is ready.
- If the receive side is not ready, the module shall assert the receive-stall status and hold all outputs and progress until the receive side becomes ready.
- The receive-byte request shall be suppressed during stalls.

For the final received byte of a segment, the module shall accompany the receive request with an end-of-segment marker. This marker shall indicate that the received byte is the last byte of the segment and that any partial receive word should be packed and made available.

### Bidirectional Segments

For a Standard bidirectional segment, the module shall:

- Request one transmit byte at the start of each byte period.
- Request one receive byte at the end of each byte period.
- Generate both transmit and receive end-of-segment markers on the final byte.

### Dummy Segments

For a dummy segment, the module shall:

- Generate SPI clock cycles for the programmed number of dummy cycles.
- Not request transmit bytes.
- Not request receive bytes.
- Not assert any data-line output enables.
- Not assert end-of-segment read or write markers.

### Shift and Sample Pulses

The module shall generate shift-enable pulses to advance the shift register by the correct number of bits for the current speed.

The module shall generate sample-enable pulses to capture incoming data at the correct point in the SPI clock period.

Both shift-enable and sample-enable pulses shall be suppressed during stalls.

## 8. Back-to-Back Segments and CSAAT

The chip-select-active-after-transaction flag, referred to as CSAAT, controls whether chip-select is deasserted at the end of a segment.

### CSAAT Cleared

If CSAAT is cleared for the current segment:

- At the end of the segment, the module shall hold the selected chip-select low for the programmed trail time.
- Then all chip-select outputs shall be driven high.
- Then the module shall wait for the programmed inter-command idle time.
- After the idle time, the module shall be ready to accept the next command.

### CSAAT Set, No Next Segment

If CSAAT is set for the current segment and no next segment is presented at the end of the segment:

- The module shall hold the selected chip-select low.
- The SPI clock shall remain idle.
- The active status shall be deasserted because no segment is being processed.
- The module shall enter a chip-select-active wait state.

While in this wait state, the module shall be ready to accept a command that targets the same chip-select.

### CSAAT Set, Next Segment Same Chip-Select

If a next command is presented with the same chip-select identifier while the module is in the chip-select-active wait state, or is presented on the final timeslice of the current segment:

- The module shall accept the command immediately.
- It shall not deassert chip-select.
- It shall not insert trail, idle, or lead delays.
- It shall reload the segment counters with the new segment length.
- It shall begin the next segment from the appropriate SPI clock state.

### CSAAT Set, Next Segment Different Chip-Select

If a next command is presented with a different chip-select identifier while the module is in the chip-select-active wait state:

- The module shall not assert command-ready on that cycle.
- Instead, it shall begin closing out the current transaction.
- The current chip-select shall remain low for the programmed trail time.
- All chip-select lines shall then be driven high.
- The module shall wait for the programmed idle time.
- After the idle time, the module shall assert command-ready and accept the waiting command.
- The command request shall remain asserted until the module accepts it.
- The new command shall then proceed with its own lead time and chip-select assertion.

## 9. Configuration Changes

The module shall support changes to the SPI configuration between transactions, such as:

- Clock polarity and phase.
- Full-cycle sampling enable.
- Clock divider.
- Chip-select lead, trail, and idle timing.

Configuration changes shall only take effect while all chip-select outputs are high.

If a newly presented command requests configuration values that differ from the currently active values, the module shall not begin the lead phase immediately. Instead, it shall:

1. Wait for any ongoing transaction to complete its trail and idle timing.
2. Apply the new configuration while all chip-select lines are high.
3. Insert an additional configuration-switch delay based on the new inter-command idle timing.
4. Only then assert the new chip-select and enter the lead phase.

This ensures that the old configuration remains valid for the old device’s required idle time and that the new configuration is stable before the new device is selected.

Configuration changes shall not be requested between two back-to-back segments while chip-select is being held active for the same transaction. Back-to-back continuation is only valid when the configuration remains unchanged.

## 10. Data-Line Output Enables

The module shall generate per-line output-enable controls for the SPI data lines.

- When all chip-select outputs are high, all data-line output enables shall be inactive.
- During TX or bidirectional segments, the output enables shall be active only on the lines used by the current speed mode:
  - Standard: only data line 0 is driven.
  - Dual: data lines 0 and 1 are driven.
  - Quad: data lines 0, 1, 2, and 3 are driven.
- During RX segments, dummy segments, and idle states, all data-line output enables shall be inactive.

For Standard-mode TX segments, the module shall hold the data-line 0 output enable active through the final bit period of the segment, even if the next segment is an RX or dummy segment. This prevents the line from floating before the last transmitted bit has completed.

For Dual and Quad TX segments, the output enables shall be active while the segment is transmitting and shall be deasserted for non-transmit portions of the segment.

## 11. Stall Behavior

The module shall support two stall conditions:

- Transmit stall: asserted when the module needs to request a transmit byte, but the transmit side is not ready.
- Receive stall: asserted when the module needs to deliver a received byte, but the receive side is not ready.

While either stall condition is active:

- The SPI clock shall hold its current level.
- Chip-select outputs shall hold their current state.
- All transfer counters shall hold their current values.
- All output pulses, including transmit requests, receive requests, sample-enable, shift-enable, and command-ready, shall be suppressed.
- The module shall resume normal operation only after the stall condition is removed.

Stall conditions are not asserted merely because no command is pending. They indicate that an otherwise active transfer is being held back by the datapath.

## 12. Active Status

The active status output shall indicate whether the module is processing a command segment or otherwise not available in the ordinary idle sense.

The active status shall be asserted during:

- Chip-select lead time.
- SPI clock active states.
- Chip-select trail time.
- Inter-command idle wait time.
- Configuration-switch delay.

The active status shall be deasserted:

- In the ordinary idle state.
- In the chip-select-active wait state, where chip-select is held low but no segment is currently being processed.

## 13. Valid Command Requirements

The module assumes that command inputs are well-formed.

The following requirements shall be satisfied by the surrounding logic or software:

- The selected chip-select identifier shall be less than the number of chip-select lines.
- The speed mode shall be Standard, Dual, or Quad; reserved speed values shall not be used.
- Bidirectional segments shall only be requested in Standard mode.
- Configuration changes shall not be requested while a chip-select-active transaction is open.

The module behavior is only defined for these valid command conditions.
